title: Feature-level microbudget & price-sensitivity simulation
content:
Purpose:
Small, feature-scoped budget model for Q4 2025 -> Q2 2026. Designed to: (a) show revenue/margin sensitivity to small price moves by feature (chat, embeddings, rerank), (b) map headcount triggers for infra/serving/SRE/customer success, and (c) recommend short-term commit vs burst mix given elasticity.

High-level assumptions (editable cells):
- USD exchange baseline: 1.00
- Avg price per 1k tokens (hosted): Chat = $0.018, Embeddings = $0.0025, Rerank = $0.045
- Token bands: Small (0-1k), Medium (1k-10k), Large (10k+) with % distribution per feature
- Baseline GAAP COGS (per-token compute + infra): Chat 60%, Embeddings 40%, Rerank 70% of price
- Customer growth (QoQ): +12% baseline; scenario A conservative +6%, B baseline +12%, C aggressive +20%
- Average FTE fully-burdened cost: Infra Eng $260k, Serving Eng $240k, SRE $230k, CS $150k

Sheet: Feature-level P&L (example rows shown)
Columns: Scenario | Price delta | Traffic delta | Revenue | COGS | Gross margin | Marg% | HC additions (next 3 months) | Opex delta | Notes

Example rows: 
- Chat | 0% | +12% | $1,120,000 | $672,000 | $448,000 | 40% | +0.8 Serving FTE | +$208k | momentum in PLG signups
- Embeddings | +10% | +8% | $420,000 | $168,000 | $252,000 | 60% | +0.2 Infra FTE | +$32k | price elasticity low
- Rerank | -5% | +20% | $310,000 | $217,000 | $93,000 | 30% | +0.5 SRE | +$85k | enterprise pilot pickup

Sensitivity matrix (price moves vs elasticity):
- Price delta tested: -20%, -10%, -5%, 0%, +5%, +10%, +20%, +30%
- Elasticities: Chat (-0.6), Embeddings (-0.2), Rerank (-1.1) (elasticity = % traffic change / % price change)
- Model note: small price increases on low-elasticity embeddings lift margin without severe volume loss; rerank is highly elastic (price up -> volume drops substantially).

Micro-forecast calculations (cell descriptions so this can be copy/pasted into a sheet):
- Revenue = baseline_revenue * (1 + traffic_delta) * (1 + price_delta)
- COGS = Revenue * feature_cogs_pct
- Gross margin = Revenue - COGS
- HC_trigger = if(projected_90d_traffic > capacity_threshold, ceil((projected_90d_traffic - capacity_threshold) / fte_throughput), 0)
- Reserve_commit_recommendation = if(expected_high_margin_months >= 3 and price_discount_on_commit < 18%, recommend 30–60% commit)

Headcount plan (rolling 6 months) - prioritized hires and trigger logic:
- Serving engineers (latency/throughput): add 1 FTE per additional sustained 80M tokens/day load above baseline. Ramp window = 60 days.
- Infra (GPU ops / capacity): add 1 Infra FTE when burst-to-reserve ratio > 45% for > 30 days (we need ops expertise to optimize VM packing/quant profiles).
- SRE: add 0.5 FTE per new enterprise pilot > $25k MRR with SLA requirements.
- CS: hire 1 CSM per 12 enterprise pilots in onboarding queue.

Cost phasing example table (numbers are illustrative):
- Q4 2025 planned hires: 2 Serving, 0 Infra, 1 CS -> incremental run-rate +$650k annualized -> cash impact Q4 = $162.5k
- Q1 2026 contingency hires (if scenario C): +3 Infra, +1 SRE -> incremental run-rate +$1.05M -> need $350k runway buffer

Price sensitivity outputs (summary for leadership):
- Best short-term lever: +5% on embeddings with projected +5% revenue lift and <1% traffic loss, gross margin +3.1pp.
- Danger zone: +10% on rerank reduces ARR by ~9% (scenario B) due to churn on enterprise pilots.
- Commit vs burst: committing 40% of expected baseline for 12 months at 12% discount yields unit cost reduction of ~18% vs on-demand; breakeven case when utilization >65% consistently.

Action items and TODOs:
- [ ] Validate elasticity numbers with product analytics (Priya) -> Confluence link in linked_artifacts.
- [ ] Run stress sims with 1k Monte Carlo draws for token-distribution tails (Marcus)
- [ ] Update per-FTE burden numbers to include Q1 2026 benefit resets (People Ops)
- [ ] Draft micro-commit offer for sales to test in next 6 enterprise demos (Sales Ops + Finance)

Open questions / notes to self:
- How do we attribute shared cache savings across features? Current model allocates pro rata by token volume which biases chat low (chat benefits disproportionately from prefix cache). Need infra input.
- Should we model a minimum viable commit product (30-day rolling reserve) to test convert rates? If yes, add a churn delta of -2pp expected.
- Link to capacity model: "shared_drives/engineering/serving-runtime/capacity-token-model-2025-10" (placeholder)

Appendix: quick sensitivity snapshot (values for leadership slide):
- Scenario B (baseline): Total revenue (next 12m) = $24.3M, COGS = $14.8M, Gross margin = $9.5M (39.1%)
- Scenario A (conservative): Total revenue = $21.1M (-13%), margin = 35% -> hiring pause on non-critical infra until Q2
- Scenario C (aggressive): Total revenue = $29.6M (+22%), margin = 41% -> recommend 4m reserved commit + hire window for infra (2-3 FTEs)
